property_summary: A call to forward must never revert if the sub-call succeeds, but must revert if the sub-call fails
forward must revert whenever the inner call to callee fails
A call to forward reverts if and only if the inner sub-call fails.
A call to forward must revert exactly when the provided callee does not have code.
A call to forward reverts exactly when the callee has no code.
A failed external call in forward must revert the transaction; the bug removes the require so a failed sub-call completes silently, leaving the contract's state unchanged but not reverting.
A call to forward must revert if the low-level callee.call fails (returns false) due to the require statement; the buggy version silently succeeds without reverting.
The forward function reverts when callee is a contract with no fallback, unless callee equals msg.sender.
The forward function reverts if and only if the low-level call to the provided callee fails.
The forward function reverts if and only if the callee's balance changes.
A low-level call to a contract with a fallback function changes the callee's balance exactly when the call does not revert.
C.forward reverts if and only if the callee's balance changes.

The contract must execute a low-level call to the provided callee address, not to msg.sender; the mutant incorrectly routes the call to msg.sender, so with a non-EOA callee that reverts any call, the reference reverts while the mutant succeeds silently.

For any callee address that is not the caller, calling forward forwards the call to that callee; the bug incorrectly calls the caller instead, so when the callee is a contract that reverts, the reference reverts but the mutant succeeds.

For any non-zero callee address that is not the caller, if the callee is a contract that reverts on call, the reference forward reverts while the mutant incorrectly calls msg.sender and succeeds, violating the rule that forward must revert when the target callee reverts.
A call to forward must result in a successful call to the provided callee, not to the contract itself.
Calling forward does not fail when the target (callee) is different from the contract itself.
A call to forward must not result in a revert.
Calling forward with a callee different from c and this contract must not revert.
A call to forward must not revert.

After any forward call, the contract's own balance never decreases; the bug version that calls address(this) can only move funds within itself, but the incorrect target makes the balance decrease when the original sends Ether to the callee.
A successful forward call that sends Ether to a non-zero callee must decrease the contract's own balance, but the mutant that calls address(this) instead leaves the balance unchanged.
After a forward call, the contract's self-call will not change its balance, whereas the correct call to an external callee may decrease it if Ether is sent.

For any forward call, if the target callee reverts, the forward fails reverting; the mutant which calls address(this) will not proceed to a revert from an external callee because no external call is made.

For any initial contract balance and any call to forward with a callee that succeeds but returns data, the reference contract forwards the call to the callee and leaves the contract's own code unchanged, while the mutant calls itself and may corrupt its own bytecode, making the contract unusable afterward.
The callee receives the exact calldata passed to forward
